summary: Controller console redesign (slices 1-5 and 7): labelled icon rail, scope/search/activity top bar, pool overview dashboard, filterable VM and host lists with slide-over panels, stacked pool settings, Tasks and Events pages, phase-gated Backups/Containers/Snapshots/Migrate/HA elements in an honest not-yet-available state, the VM tag editor and Tags facet, host uptime and NIC link-speed port tiles; the old toolbar, resource tree, detail tabs and Tasks strip are removed. Guide, browser review harness, phase 1 browser assertions and QA report updated to the new UI. Owner feedback round (2026-09-23): Storage and Networks become operational screens with per-host access lights (Settings keeps Overview, Members, High availability, Backup repositories and Updates; old storage, ISO and networks settings links redirect), Containers is a smaller rail sub-item under VMs, Overview widgets collapse to a one-line summary, the utilisation chart gains hover and keyboard reading, monotone smoothing and averaged 1D/1W/1M buckets, long notes move behind About disclosures, the VM guest tools block becomes a status grid, and Members becomes a pool status strip plus one compact row per host with status checks and a Details expander; the VM list gains a Network filter.

guide.reason: Every GUI navigation step changed (rail, scope menu, lists, slide-over panel tabs and quick actions, settings sections). Two pages added: navigating the console and tagging VMs. Feedback round: Storage/Networks/ISO locations, Settings sections, the Members status checks and Details (replacing the Fencing, Authority copy, Maintenance and Convergence columns and the Why link), the guest tools grid, Overview collapse and chart reading.

api.reason: The UI reuses the existing Controller reads and writes (sites, pools, hosts, vms, storage, networks, media, operations, audit, host/VM stats, host hardware and network, pool members, updates, VM power/media/update/delete, host revoke/probe/add, enrollment tokens). Overview totals, filters, search, placement map and attention list are computed in the browser. The VM tags field is the changed contract recorded in docs/changes/2026-09-23-vm-tags.json; host uptime_seconds and NIC speed_mbps are the inventory fields recorded in docs/changes/2026-09-23-host-nic-speed-uptime.json. No endpoint is added here. The feedback round adds no endpoint or field: host access lights read the existing storage member_access and network member access, and the VM Network filter reads the existing VM definitions.

roadmap.reason: Presentation change; phase-gated elements are disabled placeholders that do not change any milestone's built or outstanding status.

state.reason: The UI keeps only per-browser localStorage conveniences (nex.theme, nex.scope, nex.events-seen, nex.vm-columns, nex.overview.collapsed); none describes a pool resource and a fresh Controller needs none of them. VM tags live in the VM definition on the pool master (see the VM tags record).

verification.method: npm --prefix web test; python3 tests/integration/ui_review_browser.py against a local Controller with the labeled simulated fixture at 1440x900, 1024x768 and 390x844 in light and dark, captures inspected against docs/design/controller-console/reference.html; python3 tests/integration/phase1.py --browser (disposable Controller and agent, simulated virsh); guide steps walked in the browser against the simulated fixture; python3 scripts/check_docs.py --worktree; python3 -m unittest discover -s tests. Results, defects and limits are in the QA report. Feedback round: the same review harness with the added feedback views, the eleven CI browser checks run as .github/workflows/phase1.yml runs them, check_docs and the tests suite; results in the QA report's Feedback round section.
